answer: A stake-weighted reputation vault makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a deposit in a shared vault before it can transact, and misbehavior burns part of that deposit. Like a prism splitting one beam into many verifiable colors, the vault splits an attacker's funds across every fake identity, so creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits, not one. The fable of the free lunch ends here — reputation is earned slowly through honest work and lost fast, so a Sybil swarm bankrupts itself before it can fake trust.
